Logo Design – ALUR

A fictional portfolio concept: a logo identity for a logistics-operations platform.

ALUR — Logo Identity Study

Brand Snapshot

FieldDirection
Brand nameALUR — working name (provisional)
Brand typeB2B SaaS / logistics-technology startup (fictional portfolio concept)
ProductDigital operations platform for SME distributors, online sellers and local delivery operators
Main functionsOrder consolidation · route planning · dispatch coordination · delivery-status visibility · basic analytics
Primary audienceMSMEs, D2C sellers, distributors, local fleet operators, logistics operations teams
PositioningA practical logistics-operations platform that helps businesses coordinate orders and deliveries more clearly
Logo architectureAbstract mark + wordmark → combination mark; symbol must work alone as app icon
StyleMinimalist, flat, geometric, corporate, technology-led, reliable

FICTIONAL / PROVISIONAL portfolio concept — name not checked for trademark, company-name, domain or social-handle availability.

Brand Strategy

Central idea

Many moving parts, one connected flow.

01  Reliable

Operationally dependable and clear.

02  Intelligent

Data-aware; organises complex workflows.

03  Efficient

Removes friction so delivery operations are easy to understand.

Brand promise

“Every delivery, in a clearer flow.”

Design principles

  • • Software, not a courier — no truck, pin, parcel box or road
  • • Calm and organised, not fast or aggressive
  • • Symbol must stand alone inside a square app icon
  • • No gradients; single-colour dark and reversed versions required

Shared: minimalist · flat · scalable · monochrome-first

Selected Concept

ALUR

Selected: A — Converging routes

Chosen because it expresses the product idea — separate routes becoming one channel — without a truck, pin or arrow. Unequal entry heights add direction, and the solid silhouette holds inside a square app icon. Risk to monitor: reading as a Y. B is generic network imagery; C is the least abstract.

Next: build on a modular grid, correct optically, test small sizes, then apply colour only after the monochrome version is approved.

Kerning / refinement status

Open spacing keeps ALUR readable at small sizes. Only global tracking was set; per-pair kerning (A–L, L–U) is an open refinement.
